source.text: בְּצֵ֣את יִ֭שְׂרָאֵל מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם בֵּ֥ית יַ֝עֲקֹ֗ב מֵעַ֥ם לֹעֵֽז׃

records.literal_gloss: When Israel went out from Egypt, [the] house of Jacob from a people of strange speech,

en.L: When Israel went out from Egypt, the house of Jacob from a people of strange speech,
en.B: When Israel left Egypt, when the house of Jacob left a people whose speech was strange to them,
en.R: Long ago the people of Israel, the family of Jacob, left Egypt, a land where people spoke a language they did not know.

fr.L: Quand Israël est sorti d’Égypte, la maison de Jacob d’un peuple au langage étrange,
fr.B: Quand Israël a quitté l’Égypte, quand la maison de Jacob a quitté un peuple dont la langue lui était étrangère,
fr.R: Il y a longtemps, le peuple d’Israël, la famille de Jacob, a quitté l’Égypte, un pays où l’on parlait une langue qu’il ne connaissait pas.

decisions.reason: The psalm retells the going out from Egypt (Exodus 12-14), the crossing of the sea and of the Jordan (Exodus 14; Joshua 3), the trembling of Sinai (Exodus 19:18) and the water from the rock (Exodus 17:6). It is sung at Passover.

decisions.choice: strange speech: speaking a language not understood
decisions.reason: The verb (la'az) is used of speaking unintelligibly. Egypt was a foreign land whose language Israel did not share (81:6).

decisions.choice: a psalm that holds back God's name
decisions.reason: The psalm speaks of "his" sanctuary (verse 2) and asks the sea and mountains what they saw, but names the Lord only in verse 7. The ancient Greek translation joins Psalms 114 and 115 as one psalm.
The sentence continues into verse 2, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.
Readable marks the event as past history.

records.literal_gloss: Judah became his sanctuary, Israel his dominion.

en.B: Judah became {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy place, Israel the realm {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rules.
en.R: God made Judah {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy home, and Israel became the kingdom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rules.

fr.L: Juda est devenu {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sanctuaire, Israël {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} domaine.
fr.B: Juda est devenu {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} lieu saint, Israël le royaume où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} règne.
fr.R: Dieu a fait de Juda {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} sainte demeure, et Israël est devenu le royaume où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} règne.

decisions.choice: his: God's, though not yet named
decisions.reason: "His" can only be God, whom the psalm names only in verse 7 (m3 at 114:1).

decisions.choice: sanctuary: a holy place, or holy possession
decisions.reason: The word (qodesh) is holiness, or a holy place. The people itself became the place of God's presence and his own possession (Exodus 19:6).
In the parallel lines Judah and Israel together stand for all the tribes.
Readable names God, to whom "his" refers (m1).

source.text: הַיָּ֣ם רָ֭אָה וַיָּנֹ֑ס הַ֝יַּרְדֵּ֗ן יִסֹּ֥ב לְאָחֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: The sea saw and fled; the Jordan turned back.

en.L: The sea saw and fled; the Jordan turned back.
en.B: The sea looked and ran away; the Jordan turned and flowed back.
en.R: The sea saw it and ran away. The Jordan River stopped and went backward.

fr.L: La mer a vu et s’est enfuie ; le Jourdain est retourné en arrière.
fr.B: La mer a regardé et s’est sauvée ; le Jourdain a fait demi-tour.
fr.R: La mer l’a vu et s’est enfuie. Le Jourdain s’est arrêté et a reculé.

decisions.choice: the sea and the Jordan: the two crossings
decisions.reason: At the start of the journey the sea split for Israel (Exodus 14:21-22); at the end the Jordan stopped flowing so they could cross into the land (Joshua 3:13-17).

decisions.choice: the sea saw and fled: creation in awe of God
decisions.reason: The sea and river are pictured as living things that saw something and ran. What they saw is answered in verse 7: the presence of the Lord (77:17).

records.literal_gloss: The mountains skipped like rams, hills like young of [the] flock.

en.L: The mountains skipped like rams, [the] hills like the young of the flock.
en.B: The mountains sprang about like rams, the hills like lambs from the flock.
en.R: The mountains jumped around like rams. The hills jumped like little lambs.

fr.L: Les montagnes ont bondi comme des béliers, les collines comme les petits du troupeau.
fr.B: Les montagnes ont sauté comme des béliers, les collines comme des agneaux du troupeau.
fr.R: Les montagnes ont sauté comme des béliers. Les collines ont sauté comme de petits agneaux.

decisions.reason: When the LORD came down on Mount Sinai, the whole mountain shook (Exodus 19:18; Judges 5:5; 68:9). The poem pictures the shaking as rams and lambs leaping.

source.text: מַה־לְּךָ֣ הַ֭יָּם כִּ֣י תָנ֑וּס הַ֝יַּרְדֵּ֗ן תִּסֹּ֥ב לְאָחֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: What [is] to you, sea, that you flee, Jordan, [that] you turn back,

en.L: What [is it] with you, sea, that you flee, Jordan, [that] you turn back,
en.B: What is wrong, sea, that you run away? Jordan, why do you turn back?
en.R: Sea, why do you run away? Jordan River, why do you turn back?

fr.L: Qu’as-tu, mer, pour t’enfuir, Jourdain, pour retourner en arrière,
fr.B: Qu’as-tu donc, mer, pour te sauver ? Jourdain, pourquoi fais-tu demi-tour ?
fr.R: Mer, pourquoi t’enfuis-tu ? Jourdain, pourquoi recules-tu ?

decisions.choice: What is it with you: a teasing question
decisions.reason: The poet speaks to the sea, river, mountains and hills as if watching it happen now and asks what has frightened them. The answer comes in verse 7.
At Literal the question continues into verse 6, so this verse ends with a comma. Balanced and Readable ask it as separate questions.

records.literal_gloss: mountains, [that] you skip like rams, hills, like young of [the] flock?

en.L: mountains, [that] you skip like rams, hills, like the young of the flock?
en.B: Mountains, why do you spring about like rams, and you hills, like lambs from the flock?
en.R: Mountains, why do you jump around like rams? Hills, why do you jump like little lambs?

fr.L: montagnes, pour bondir comme des béliers, collines, comme les petits du troupeau ?
fr.B: Montagnes, pourquoi sautez-vous comme des béliers, et vous, collines, comme des agneaux du troupeau ?
fr.R: Montagnes, pourquoi sautez-vous comme des béliers ? Collines, pourquoi sautez-vous comme de petits agneaux ?

decisions.reason: Verses 5-6 repeat verses 3-4 as questions, which builds up to the answer of verse 7.

source.text: מִלִּפְנֵ֣י אָ֭דוֹן ח֣וּלִי אָ֑רֶץ מִ֝לִּפְנֵ֗י אֱל֣וֹהַּ יַעֲקֹֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: Before [the] Lord tremble, earth, before [the] God of Jacob,

en.L: Before the Lord tremble, earth, before the God of Jacob,
en.B: Earth, shake with fear before the Lord, before the God of Jacob,
en.R: Earth, tremble when the Lord comes near! Tremble before the God of Jacob.

fr.L: Devant le Seigneur tremble, terre, devant le Dieu de Jacob,
fr.B: Terre, tremble de crainte devant le Seigneur, devant le Dieu de Jacob,
fr.R: Terre, tremble quand le Seigneur s’approche ! Tremble devant le Dieu de Jacob.

decisions.reason: The word ('adon) is "lord, master". Here, with no other name, it is God, the Lord of all the earth (97:5). The psalm does not use the divine name at all.
The verb (chul) is to shake or writhe, as in the pains of birth (29:8; 77:17). The answer to the questions is a command: all the earth should tremble as the sea and mountains did.
Here the singular word for God (Eloah) is used, which is rare in the Psalms (18:32). "Jacob" names Israel by its ancestor, as in verse 1.
The sentence continues into verse 8, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.literal_gloss: who turns the rock [into] a pool of water, flint into a spring of water.

en.L: who turns the rock [into] a pool of water, flint into a spring of water.
en.B: who changed the rock into a pool of water, and hard flint into a flowing spring.
en.R: He turned solid rock into a pool of water. He made a spring of water flow out of hard stone.

fr.L: qui change le rocher [en] étang d’eau, le silex en source d’eau.
fr.B: qui a changé le rocher en étang et le dur silex en source jaillissante.
fr.R: Il a changé un rocher en étang. Il a fait couler une source d’eau d’une pierre très dure.

decisions.choice: water from the rock in the wilderness
decisions.reason: The LORD gave Israel water from the rock at Horeb and at Meribah (Exodus 17:6; Numbers 20:11; Deuteronomy 8:15, "water from the flint rock"; 78:15-16).
The participle (hahofkhi) describes God by what he does. The earth trembles at the God who can make hard rock run with water.
